classification.difficultyReason: Maintain each intermediate point through two specified translations and read the final coordinates, tracking opposing horizontal movements and reinforcing vertical movements.

content.prompt: Plot the following points on your graph paper. First translate them 1 unit up and 3 units to the right, and then translate the images 2 units up and 2 units to the left. State the coordinates of the final images.

answer.worked: On graph paper, move $A$ 3 units right and 1 unit up to $A'(4,-1)$. Then move $A'$ 2 units left and 2 units up to $A''(2,1)$.
On graph paper, move $B$ 3 units right and 1 unit up to $B'(-2,-2)$. Then move $B'$ 2 units left and 2 units up to $B''(-4,0)$.
On graph paper, move $C$ 3 units right and 1 unit up to $C'(2,5)$. Then move $C'$ 2 units left and 2 units up to $C''(0,7)$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 14; completed plotting supported by teacher PDF page 58
spec.description: One shared coordinate plane shows every original point, first image and final image. Labels identify points; coordinates appear in the individual answers.
spec.mathematics: First translation (x,y) to (x+3,y+1); second translation to (x+1,y+3). A: (1,-2), (4,-1), (2,1). B: (-5,-3), (-2,-2), (-4,0). C: (-1,4), (2,5), (0,7). Grid step is one coordinate unit on each axis.
